title: Protecting tropical forests is more cost-effective for biodiversity and climate than restoration.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data file could be opened because none was found. I checked: Europe PMC (isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, no PMCID, so no full text, no data-availability statement and no supplementary file listing); Unpaywall (oa_status 'closed', best_oa_location null, has_repository_copy false); Crossref (no 'relation' entries, i.e. no linked dataset DOI); science.org returned HTTP 403 so the article page and its supplementary materials were unreachable; Zenodo API (searches on 'adx9928', on Amazon cost-effectiveness/restoration titles, on 'Sustainable Amazon Network', and on the first author) = 0 relevant hits; Dryad API on the DOI = 0; Harvard Dataverse = 0; Figshare = 0 relevant; DataCite = 0 for the DOI as a query term and 0 for any record citing this DOI as a related identifier; the INPE institutional record timed out twice.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the study design comes from the abstract and press coverage only: field assessments plus high-resolution remote sensing over the Santarem and Paragominas regions of Para, Brazil (reported as >3 million hectares, 2010-2020), comparing observed versus counterfactual biodiversity and carbon outcomes and costs for avoided deforestation, avoided disturbance and restoration. I saw no row counts, no plot counts, no column names and no units.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. No public data location could be found anywhere. The article is fully closed (Unpaywall 'closed', no repository copy, no PubMed Central record), science.org blocks automated access (HTTP 403) so even the data-availability statement is unreadable, and no dataset deposit exists in Zenodo, Dryad, Figshare, Harvard Dataverse or DataCite (including a search for any record that names this DOI as a related identifier). Per the rules, an unreachable download is an A1 failure.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not verifiable, and the likely answer is no. The quantity of interest is a counterfactual benefit (what biodiversity or carbon would have been without the intervention), which by definition is not measured but constructed by the authors' own statistical model from field plots plus satellite maps.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verifiable; no file listing was obtainable.

a4_units_stated.note: Not verifiable; no data dictionary or file header was obtainable.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unknown and probably small at the unit that matters. The analysis unit for the field component is the forest plot; the Sustainable Amazon Network surveys behind this region are on the order of a few hundred plots, far below the ~1,500-row bar, though I could not verify any count.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not verifiable. Plot tables would be tiny; the high-resolution remote-sensing layers over 3 million hectares would not be, but neither was accessible.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare: there is no download and no accessible full text to take counts from.

a8_label_provenance.note: Serious concern even in principle. The headline outcomes are counterfactual (modelled) biodiversity and carbon differences and modelled intervention costs, i.e. outputs of the authors' own models rather than direct measurements, so a model trained on them would be distilling their model, not learning the ecology.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the underlying data could not be located or opened, so nothing about this paper's measurements can be modelled or checked.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use satellite images of Amazon forest patches to predict their species richness and stored carbon.
plain_idea.train_on: Field-surveyed forest plots in Para, Brazil, each paired with satellite-derived descriptions of the surrounding forest (canopy cover, disturbance history, distance to edge). Number of plots: unknown, none verified.
plain_idea.predict: Plot-level biodiversity (species counts for plants, birds and beetles) and above-ground carbon stock, measured by on-the-ground survey crews and tree-trunk measurements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Conservation funders choosing between protecting and replanting forest need per-hectare benefit estimates; a model mapping cheap satellite data to expensive field measurements would let them score land parcels without a field campaign.

ml_idea: Intended idea: map freely available satellite and landscape features to field-measured biodiversity and carbon in Amazonian forest plots, then use the model to score unsurveyed parcels for conservation value. Not pursuable here because no data file from this paper is obtainable.

effort.compute_note: No estimates possible: no files, no counts and no formats were observable.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a data-availability statement naming a public repository. I checked Zenodo, Dryad, Figshare, Dataverse and DataCite (including related-identifier links to the DOI) and found nothing; that alone kills it, and took about ten minutes.

verdict_reason: Part A1: the paper is fully paywalled with no open-access or repository copy, the publisher blocks automated access so the data-availability statement is unreadable, and no dataset deposit exists in any major repository. Secondary concerns even if the data appeared: the outcomes are modelled counterfactuals rather than direct measurements (A8), and the field-plot sample size is almost certainly in the hundreds, not thousands (A5).
